title: Four client predicates for "rules in force" still disagree on the signature
body:
## Summary
Whether a rule set is in force is decided four times on the client; after d2face5 Settings and Agent rules agree (signed, no refusal, in its dates), but the Charter (lib/firstRun.ts) still ignores the owner signature and setup/circuit.ts documents a premise that is false.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/rules/RulesLayer.tsx:42 inForce = active && owner_sig && !refusal; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/limits.ts:44 rulesAnswer = window && owner_sig && !refusal; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/settings/SettingsLayer.tsx circuitMandates = owner_sig && !refusal, then setup/circuit.ts:83 mandatesInForce adds the window; apps/desktop/client/src/lib/firstRun.ts:96 rulesInForce = window && !refusal (no signature). setup/circuit.ts:82 says "mandate_list already returns only active rows", which is false: mandate_list returns ended, refused and unsigned rows (Agent rules lists them as Not in force). Fixed: one exported predicate (e.g. lib/mandateRules.ts or setup/limits.ts) used by all four sites, and the circuit comment corrected.

## Flow
- a mandate_list row with owner_sig [] inside its dates
- Agent rules: not in force (red "not signed" chip); Settings: rules step missing (since d2face5); Charter line II: done
- fix: shared inForce(entry, now); firstRun, limits, circuit and RulesLayer call it; correct circuit.ts:82

## Expected impact
The first-run Charter stops ticking the rules line for a set that allows nothing. Could break: Charter tests that build entries without owner_sig.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of "in force" on the client
Before: 4 predicates, 1 (firstRun) accepts an unsigned set; 1 comment states a false premise
After: predicted 1 predicate, 4 call sites
Method: simulation - the remaining sites are lib/firstRun.ts (client-foundation) and setup/* (another context); walked on the code
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/firstRun.ts:96-98 `... && !m.refusal` (no owner_sig)
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/limits.ts:44 `... && m.owner_sig.length > 0 && !m.refusal`
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/rules/RulesLayer.tsx:42
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/setup/circuit.ts:82 `(mandate_list already returns only active rows)`
instrument: one vitest over a matrix {active, ended, not yet, refused, unsigned} x {firstRun rulesInForce, limits rulesAnswer, circuit via circuitMandates+mandatesInForce, RulesLayer inForce}: all four agree; red today on the unsigned row (firstRun says in force)

title: Tokenise the Rewind glyph sizes in rewind.css
body:
## Summary
rewind.css sets six glyph and caption sizes in raw px (15px, 16px, max(12px..)) beside the --fs-* tokens.

## Description
The area header says text never goes below --fs-small (12px). Checked every raw size in apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/rewind.css: 15px (rw-nav chevron), 15px/16px (refusal x glyph), max(15px..), max(12px..), max(18px..). All are at or above the 12px floor; the x and chevrons are glyphs, not text.

## Flow
- grep raw px font sizes in rewind.css
- compare each with --fs-small (design/tokens.css:98, 12px)

## Expected impact
None: the stated rule already holds.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - text never under the floor
Before: 0 of 6 raw sizes under 12px
After: 0 of 6 (a token swap changes no figure)
Method: probe - grep over rewind.css against tokens.css
Result: not-better
Gate: none
